FOR YOUR SAFETY...
PACIFIC COAST AIRLINES suggests that you take a moment before the takeoff to
familiarize yourself with our pressurized Jetstream. Note the location and operations of the
exits, seat belts, and other safety equipment. FIND OUT HOW TO GET YOURSELF OUT
OF THE AIRCRAFT quickly should it become necessary-to do so.
Pacific Coast flights are operated by a Captain and First Officer that are certified and
trained in accordance with stringent federal regulations. In the highly unlikely event that an
emergency were to occur on this flight, the most important thing to remember is to remain
calm and FOLLOW THE INSTRUCTIONS OF A CREWMEMBER. Most aircraft accidents
are survivable as long as the passenger does not panic.

ABOUT THE AIRCRAFT...
The Handley Page Jetstream is a pressurized jetprop airliner capable of cruising at speeds
of around 300 mph and at an altitude of 25,000 feet. The Jetstream is equipped to the same
standard as a modern large jetliner, including radar, anti-icing, and other systems, for all-
weather operations.
The turboprop engines on the Jetstream propel the aircraft directly, by means of the
exhaust thrust, and indirectly, by means of turbine wheels which trap the jet energy and
drive the propeller. This arrangement combines the light weight and reliability advantages
of the pure jet with the fuel efficiency and performance of the propeller for short flights.
The Jetstream is a good neighbor, too, with relatively low noise levels during takeoff and
landing. Short runways that are not adequate for a jet aircraft can safely be used by the
Jetstream, and it is capable of taking off and landing with either one of its two engines shut
down.
FOR THE INFREQUENT TRAVELER:
If you travel by air infrequently, you may be unacquainted with some of the sights and
sounds common to all airline travel.
During the taxi for departure, on days when the temperature and humidity of the air are just
right, you may notice condensation in the aisle: this "fog" is associated with the normal
operation of the air conditioning system, and will disappear after a short time.
During the takeoff, the airplane will climb steeply away from the ground, and may
occasionally bank into a turn, in order to minimize the noise level on the ground. On the
approach, the flight crew may also elect to use a steep approach to minimize exposure to
low altitude turbulence and thus increase passenger comfort. Immediately after takeoff
and just before landing, hydraulic systems will operate the landing gear with
accompanying whines and thumps.
In the interest of safety, the angle of the propeller blades on the Jetstream are changed
during the landing in order to reverse the air flow and slow the aircraft as quickly as
possible in all kinds of weather conditions. This allows the airplane to be completely
stopped without the use of its brakes.
The NO SMOKING and FASTEN SEAT BELT signs must be observed whenever they are
illuminated. When the seat belt sign is off, you may move about the cabin freely; however,
while you are in your seat it is wise to keep your seatbelt fastened to guard against
unexpected turbulence. Most of your flights aboard the Jetstream will be smooth: Pacific
Coast usually flies at the "middle" altitudes where year-round turbulence is minimized
FEDERAL REGULATIONS do not permit passengers to operate any type of radio or
electronic game on board U.S. airliners, as they may interfere with the navigational
equipment on the aircraft. Pocket tape recorders or calculators may be used. No person
may drink an alcoholic beverage on an airline flight unless it has been served to him by that
airline, and no airline may serve a passenger if that passenger appears to be intoxicated.
It is a felony to interfere with or assault any flight crewmember aboard an aircraft: in
addition, the Captain of the aircraft is in authority over the aircraft, its passengers and its
crew, from the time that the aircraft is boarded until it is deplaned.
